ranking_metric: deps.dev directDependentCount summed over all releases
selection: JCodec (76), MP3SPI (55), JLayer (33), jaudiotagger (8) and mp3agic (6) have comparable summed deps.dev direct-dependent metrics and exact outputs on two valid untagged Layer III controls. The first three decode PCM; jaudiotagger verifies first-frame header fields, and mp3agic verifies header fields from its local-file scan. Each has own Java parser source-line coverage and stable parser-derived AFL++ feedback.
family_note: JCodec and JLayer are independent decoders; MP3SPI delegates to a JLayer fork. jaudiotagger and mp3agic have their own MPEG header code, each already present as the same package in the tagged-MP3 cell; jid3lib shares historical ancestry with them.
uncertainty: Five pure-Java Layer III paths verified; no padding. jaudiotagger is first-header-only and mp3agic reports only accurate header fields. Both higher-level APIs misidentify the valid 22.05 kHz control start at byte 104 and estimate 5 rather than 12 frames; mp3agic reports 261 ms versus oracle about 313 ms. These paths make no whole-file frame-count or duration claim. Maven Central phrase queries returned no hits, so named leads were inspected via deps.dev and package documentation. deps.dev counts whole-package dependency use, not MP3-specific calls. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5 or ID3 behavior. Java SE 25 exports no MP3 reader by inventory.
